evidence.exact_quote: This document is a **boundary map**, not an implementation plan.

items.impact: Provides a deterministic owner-routing layer and prevents consumer documents from becoming accidental schema owners.
items.statement: The prologue clearly limits Crosswalk to primitive ownership and precedence routing, repeatedly distinguishing owner documents from presentation and consumer surfaces.
items.title: Boundary-map authority is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: If route is ambiguous (e.g., `~/output` with no scheme), the active Persona's default route is used.

items.impact: A malformed or ambiguous destination can be resolved differently by builders, potentially creating data in an unintended workspace or attempting an unauthorized external write without a falsifiable failure contract.
items.statement: The route cascade names permission, authentication, and integration preconditions but does not specify validation, confirmation, offline behavior, retry boundaries, atomicity, or user-visible recovery for ambiguous and failing routes.
items.title: Route fallback lacks safety and recovery semantics

evidence.exact_quote: feature/surface docs may consume these states but MUST NOT redefine the axes or collapse them into one field

items.impact: Prevents UI consumers from masking stale data as unhealthy data or collapsing distinct mutation-gating conditions.
items.statement: Projection freshness and health are explicitly orthogonal, with storage, decision, and GUI ownership separated.
items.title: Projection axes are protected from consumer drift

evidence.exact_quote: Missing `usage_event_ref` definition is a hard blocker for trust-safe cross-surface navigation.

items.impact: Usage deep links cannot be implemented or tested consistently until identity shape and ownership are defined.
items.statement: The rewrite-era routing prose explicitly acknowledges that usage_event_ref remains undefined while downstream route consumers already depend on it.
items.title: Usage event route identity is a declared blocker

evidence.exact_quote: Re-anchoring is deterministic: 1) position selector match, else 2) quote selector match using prefix/suffix preference, else 3) keep the annotation open and surface `Anchor not found — reselect to re-anchor`.

items.impact: Gives builders a deterministic fallback and honest UI state when a persisted annotation anchor becomes stale.
items.statement: Document annotations define exact operations, lifecycle, dual selectors, conflict exclusion, deterministic re-anchoring, and a visible unrecoverable-anchor state.
items.title: Annotation re-anchoring has an exact recovery ladder

evidence.exact_quote: Overlapping mutating annotations conflict by default and are excluded from automatic targeted revision until resolved.

items.impact: Concurrent edits or sensitive selections may be reconciled, retained, or exposed inconsistently, and partial targeted revisions may not be safely attributable.
items.statement: Conflict exclusion is stated, but no conflict detector version, optimistic concurrency token, merge ordering, access-control rule, sensitive-text retention limit, or audit attribution contract is given.
items.title: Annotation conflicts lack concurrency and privacy contracts

evidence.exact_quote: Multi-Pass Review is final-review only: enabled only when all bundle docs are Approved/Done and no durable annotations remain open.

items.impact: Prevents premature final review and makes pending comment/question annotations semantically blocking.
items.statement: The final-review gate has a crisp entry condition, pending chat chips cannot bypass it, reruns require explicit action, and the final decision is constrained to Accept, Reject, or Edit.
items.title: Final review entry is deterministically gated

evidence.exact_quote: Crosswalk uses primitive names as routing labels only; detailed schemas belong

items.impact: The PlanUnits preserve scope, precedence, naming, and route-owner boundaries without compiling work nodes.
items.statement: C-002 through C-007 faithfully atomize canonical owner-section status, naming, boundary scope, precedence, primitive routing, and the GUI/CLI route cascade.
items.title: Foundational Crosswalk PlanUnits preserve owner boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: CLI -r/--route and GUI Save actions resolve route_target strings through the documented cascade.

items.impact: Implementations can disagree on malformed schemes, inaccessible files, missing auth, network loss, integration absence, or implicit creation behavior.
items.statement: C-007 tests successful cascade selection but supplies no acceptance criteria for invalid route strings, permission denial, authentication failure, offline operation, rollback, or prevention of unintended writes.
items.title: C-007 lacks adversarial route-resolution oracles

evidence.exact_quote: python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate

items.impact: Passing migration/index validation does not demonstrate that GUI, CLI, persona, or external route consumers implement identical behavior.
items.statement: All six PlanUnits rely on the same migration and index validators, with no executable cross-surface or contract-conformance oracle named.
items.title: Foundational units rely on structural validation only

evidence.exact_quote: Feature and surface docs do not redefine or collapse the axes.

items.impact: Open, file realization, worktree, projection, subagent, and HITL consumers receive explicit non-overlapping owner boundaries.
items.statement: C-008 through C-014 consistently route canonical behavior to Contracts, FileManager, Source Control, assistant chat, storage, orchestration, and HITL owners while constraining consumers.
items.title: Navigation and runtime ownership split is internally coherent

evidence.exact_quote: GUI Open and Inspect actions normalize requests to OpenSubject.

items.impact: A GUI can expose enabled Open or Inspect actions yet fail silently, misroute an unsupported subject, or strand keyboard and assistive-technology users without recovery focus.
items.statement: C-008 defines supported types and normalization but not malformed/unknown subject handling, authorization failures, unavailable resolvers, offline state, error disclosure, or post-failure focus behavior.
items.title: OpenSubject normalization omits negative-path GUI truth

evidence.exact_quote: Thread-to-worktree binding is owned by assistant-chat-design.md.

items.impact: Concurrent bind, unbind, deletion, merge-back, or restart operations can produce ambiguous ownership or a stale thread-to-worktree join.
items.statement: C-011 names the 1:1 binding owner and consumers but does not define compare-and-swap semantics, collision resolution, deletion behavior, restart reconciliation, or merge-back partial-failure recovery.
items.title: Thread-worktree binding lacks race resolution

evidence.exact_quote: freshness=current|refreshing|stale
health=healthy|degraded|unavailable

items.impact: Makes stale-but-healthy and current-but-degraded representations possible without consumer reinterpretation.
items.statement: C-012 preserves exact independent state vocabularies and assigns persistence, gating, and presentation to distinct owners.
items.title: Projection state vocabulary is exact and orthogonal

evidence.exact_quote: Provider-specific transport/capability docs must not own global selection precedence.

items.impact: Separates debug, permission, remediation, provider, terminal, pressure, and rewrite-era owner families without granting consumers schema authority.
items.statement: C-015 through C-021 preserve a deliberate multi-owner topology and explicit negative constraints against ownership collapse.
items.title: Cross-cutting runtime authorities remain separated

evidence.exact_quote: Provider pressure projection records Observed effective versus Inferred only and normalized pressure fields.

items.impact: Schedulers and GUIs can derive different hard-block or resolution outcomes from the same provider evidence, especially during stale, missing, or contradictory observations.
items.statement: C-020 preserves pressure field names but does not define thresholds, evidence freshness, precedence between observed and inferred values, sampling cadence, provider disagreement, unavailable-provider behavior, or executable projection oracles.
items.title: Provider pressure fields lack derivation semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Append-after-references drift is a structural owner-doc failure, not a new source of truth.

items.impact: Consumers may misread post-References material or duplicate numbering as a separate or lower-authority source until structural cleanup is enforced.
items.statement: C-021 correctly preserves declared structural debt, but its acceptance criteria only require visibility and do not name a closure oracle for duplicate numbering, primitive-index completeness, or post-References placement.
items.title: Owner-doc structural debt is preserved but not closed

evidence.exact_quote: Wrapper commands remain useful surface verbs but not the universal navigation primitive.

items.impact: Surface state, account/persona/model routing, route identity, worktree history, Orchestrator IA, wrapper commands, and approval flows remain consumers of shared owners.
items.statement: C-022 through C-028 form a coherent normalization family around shared route/open identity and explicit GUI ownership seams.
items.title: Route consumers are normalized without becoming owners

evidence.exact_quote: Historical lane/worktree records survive archive, prune, and remove.

items.impact: Survival through destructive cleanup may conflict with privacy deletion, repository removal, storage limits, or authorization revocation, and no tombstone/redaction behavior is defined.
items.statement: C-025 requires durable lineage after archive, prune, and remove but omits retention duration, redaction, right-to-delete, tombstones, encryption, authorization checks, and behavior when referenced repositories or worktrees disappear.
items.title: Historical worktree survival lacks lifecycle policy

evidence.exact_quote: Cross-tab routes preserve filter/select target context instead of merely switching tabs.

items.impact: Deep links may preserve data context while losing keyboard focus, screen-reader announcement, scroll position, or stable localized labels, producing a misleading navigation success.
items.statement: C-026 specifies tab responsibilities and route context but no accessibility focus contract, announcement behavior, keyboard ordering, localization-safe identifiers, or executable cross-tab GUI oracle.
items.title: Orchestrator cross-tab routing omits accessible focus semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Command-specific payloads normalize to the shared route model.

items.impact: A wrapper can normalize successfully but fail during target lookup, authorization, destination loading, or context restoration with no required effective-outcome disclosure.
items.statement: C-027 defines normalization authority but not dispatch acknowledgement, requested-versus-effective target reporting, timeout behavior, idempotency, partial restoration, telemetry, or user-visible recovery.
items.title: Wrapper command normalization lacks outcome semantics

evidence.exact_quote: SCM/runtime flows replace tier-bound worktree identity with the lane/worktree plus execution-context model.

items.impact: The final core window consistently routes scheduler, operational identity, usage, history, migration, and annotation behavior while protecting shared identities.
items.statement: C-029 through C-034 preserve the intended graph/package/lane/route and durable-annotation owner boundaries and explicitly reject tier and raw-path regressions.
items.title: Execution and identity migration direction is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: One scheduler truth is required across the listed owner docs.

items.impact: Builders can still select incompatible lexicographic, scored, or UI-derived scheduling and recovery behavior while satisfying the stated requirement that only one be chosen.
items.statement: C-029 identifies a scheduler-truth split but neither selects the canonical algorithm nor defines tie-breaking, fairness, replan authority, recovery ordering, concurrent-ready-node semantics, or executable equivalence tests.
items.title: C-029 requires one scheduler truth without defining it

evidence.exact_quote: usage_event is a first-class routed object.

items.impact: Usage, attention, history, ledger, and deep-link consumers cannot reliably serialize, restore, authorize, or test the same routed object.
items.statement: C-031 promotes usage_event to first-class routed identity but does not close the prologue's explicit usage_event_ref blocker with fields, owner anchor, version, caller inventory, or acceptance oracle.
items.title: C-031 promotes an identity whose contract remains undefined

evidence.exact_quote: operational_identity records external side-effect target context.

items.impact: Environment targets may leak sensitive names, become stale, collide across providers, or authorize operations against the wrong target; unbounded lineage may also grow without policy.
items.statement: C-030 and C-032 elevate operational and durable route identities but omit canonical field schemas, versioning, namespace collision rules, authorization binding, redaction, retention, tombstones, cardinality limits, and stale-target handling.
items.title: Durable operational identity lacks schema and lifecycle limits

evidence.exact_quote: Tiers is retired as a primary view and route identity.

items.impact: Persisted tier links, historical records, extensions, and in-flight sessions may break or silently map to the wrong package/lane/seam after migration.
items.statement: C-033 declares the replacement model but does not define a legacy-to-new identity mapping, migration order, compatibility window, invalid legacy-state handling, rollback, telemetry, or sunset oracle.
items.title: Tier retirement lacks a migration and rollback contract

evidence.exact_quote: Anchor storage includes TextPositionSelector and TextQuoteSelector when deterministic source text exists.

items.impact: Selected text and provenance can persist sensitive content, while simultaneous revisions can yield inconsistent anchor resolution or unauthorized mutation.
items.statement: C-034 preserves annotation shape and deterministic re-anchoring but omits access control, sensitive-text redaction, retention/deletion, concurrent document-version checks, transactional multi-annotation application, and executable conflict tests.
items.title: Annotation PlanUnit omits security and race oracles

segments.summary: Reviewed precedence, primitive routing, route/open behavior, worktree and projection ownership, and exact versus adversarial failure boundaries.
Reviewed rewrite-era owner routing, explicit structural debt, document annotations, targeted revision, final review, and recovery terminology.
Reviewed runtime ownership addenda and foundational PlanUnits C-002 through C-007, including route-cascade negative paths and oracle strength.
Reviewed PlanUnits C-008 through C-014 for open normalization, path realization, worktree binding, projection state, subagent ownership, and HITL boundaries.
Reviewed PlanUnits C-015 through C-021 for debug, permissions, remediation, provider/account, terminal, pressure, and structural owner routing.
Reviewed PlanUnits C-022 through C-028 for surface state, routing identity, history retention, Orchestrator IA, wrapper dispatch, and approval flows.
Reviewed PlanUnits C-029 through C-034 for scheduler truth, operational and usage identity, durable history, tier migration, and annotation safety.
